This file contains the export helper used after the three convergence
notebooks compute the errors and construct their plots. It preserves the
mathematical labels and reference curves already present in each plot; it
performs no numerical approximation or rate fitting.

## `myggsave()`

Exports a `ggplot`-compatible object to a standalone TikZ figure, compiles
it to PDF, rasterizes that PDF to PNG, and copies the PNG to the presentation
directory. `width` and `height` are in inches, with defaults 9.22 and 7.05.
`use_mathpazo = TRUE` adds the Palatino-style LaTeX font package and the
filename suffix `_with_mathpazo`; `FALSE` omits both.

The file stem is `deparse(substitute(plot))`, so passing a named object
such as `p_h_nicer_tadpole` determines the output name directly. A named
plot object is the intended input rather than an inline plotting expression.
Outputs are:

| Artifact | Destination |
|---|---|
| Compiled vector figure | `data_files/tikzpic/<stem><suffix>.pdf` |
| Raster figure, converted at 400 dpi | `data_files/tikzpic/<stem><suffix>.png` |
| Presentation copy of the PNG | `~/Desktop/leninPresentations/data_files/<stem><suffix>.png` |

`here::here()` resolves the project output directory, which is created if
necessary. `options()` sets global TikZ document and package options.
`tikzDevice::tikz()` opens the standalone device, `print(plot)` draws the
figure, and `dev.off()` closes it. The external `pdflatex` command compiles
the intermediate `.tex`; ImageMagick's `convert` rasterizes the PDF without
trimming. Both executables, TikZ and the selected LaTeX packages must be
available, and ImageMagick must permit PDF input.

The function checks that the PNG exists after conversion and stops if it
does not. The external commands' exit statuses are not otherwise checked.
It removes the intermediate `.tex`, `.aux`, `.log`, and matching TikZ raster
fragments, creates the presentation directory if needed, and overwrites an
existing presentation PNG through `file.copy(..., overwrite = TRUE)`.
The final `cat()` reports the three output paths; the function's useful
outputs are these files and messages rather than a returned plot.

```{r}
myggsave <- function(plot,
                     width = 9.22,
                     height = 7.05,
                     use_mathpazo = TRUE) {
  
  dir_to_save <- here::here("data_files/tikzpic")
  obj_name <- deparse(substitute(plot))
  
  # --- Filename suffix ---
  suffix <- if (use_mathpazo) "_with_mathpazo" else ""
  
  tex_name <- file.path(dir_to_save, paste0(obj_name, suffix, ".tex"))
  pdf_name <- file.path(dir_to_save, paste0(obj_name, suffix, ".pdf"))
  png_name <- file.path(dir_to_save, paste0(obj_name, suffix, ".png"))
  
  # Create directory if needed
  if (!dir.exists(dir_to_save)) dir.create(dir_to_save, recursive = TRUE)

  # --- TikZ + LaTeX options ---
  tikz_packages <- c(
    "\\usepackage{tikz}",
    "\\usetikzlibrary{calc}",
    "\\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}"
  )
  
  if (use_mathpazo) {
    tikz_packages <- c(tikz_packages, "\\usepackage[sc]{mathpazo}")
  }

  options(
    tikzDocumentDeclaration = "\\documentclass[tikz,border=0pt]{standalone}",
    tikzLatexPackages = tikz_packages
  )

  # Save TikZ plot
  tikzDevice::tikz(tex_name, standAlone = TRUE, width = width, height = height)
  print(plot)
  dev.off()
  
  # Compile to PDF
  system(
    paste0("pdflatex -output-directory=", dir_to_save, " ", tex_name),
    ignore.stdout = TRUE,
    ignore.stderr = TRUE
  )
  
  # --- Convert PDF to PNG (ImageMagick, no trimming) ---
  cmd <- paste(
    "convert -density 400",
    shQuote(pdf_name),
    shQuote(png_name)
  )
  
  system(cmd, ignore.stdout = TRUE, ignore.stderr = TRUE)
  
  if (!file.exists(png_name)) {
    stop("PNG conversion failed. Likely ImageMagick PDF policy restriction.")
  }
  
  # --- Clean auxiliary files ---
  aux_ext <- c(".aux", ".log", ".tex")
  for (ext in aux_ext) {
    f <- file.path(dir_to_save, paste0(obj_name, suffix, ext))
    if (file.exists(f)) file.remove(f)
  }
  
  ras_files <- list.files(
    dir_to_save,
    pattern = paste0(obj_name, suffix, "_ras[0-9]+\\.png$"),
    full.names = TRUE
  )
  if (length(ras_files) > 0) file.remove(ras_files)
  
  # --- Copy PNG to presentation folder ---
  pres_dir <- path.expand("~/Desktop/leninPresentations/data_files")
  if (!dir.exists(pres_dir)) dir.create(pres_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  
  pres_png <- file.path(pres_dir, basename(png_name))
  file.copy(png_name, pres_png, overwrite = TRUE)
  
  # --- Output ---
  cat("PDF saved at:", pdf_name, "\n",
      "PNG saved at:", png_name, "\n",
      "PNG copied to:", pres_png, "\n")
}
```
